title: Tokyo Marathon 2026 Official Program Guidebook — During the Race (p.29)
claims: The course has nine cut-off checkpoints, and runners should refer to page 24 for their times and locations.
Runners who are cut off or withdraw should follow race officials to the finish area on the sweep bus, or return home from the nearest station.
Runners who checked in baggage must board the sweep bus to return to the finish area.
To withdraw, a runner should notify a race official, remove the barcode from the bib and hand it to the official, then proceed to the nearest checkpoint.
There are 15 aid stations along the course, and personal drinks stations are available only to elite athletes.
The organiser accepts no responsibility for fluids or food taken outside the official aid stations.
Rubbish from the aid stations must go into the bins provided, and bins are only for waste produced at that station.
Race officials may cut off runners outside the formal checkpoints if they judge that the runner may not reach the finish in time.
